message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep completed for the monitored products in Products.txt, covering the last 24 hours ending with the scheduled run on 2026-06-17 05:10 IST. Confirmed relevant findings were found for Mozilla Firefox and Ubuntu. Two fresh vendor-family items for Cisco SD-WAN Manager and FortiSandbox are included as possible matches needing review because they do not directly match the exact monitored Cisco Nexus/UCS/Fabric Extender or FortiGate/FortiOS product names.

**Finding 1: Mozilla Firefox 152 and Firefox ESR security fixes**

- Product: Mozilla Firefox / Firefox ESR
- Issue: Multiple CVEs fixed in Firefox 152 and Firefox ESR 140.12, including CVE-2026-12289, CVE-2026-12290, CVE-2026-12291, CVE-2026-12294 through CVE-2026-12299, CVE-2026-12326, CVE-2026-12327, CVE-2026-12328, and CVE-2026-12329.
- Severity: High overall, as stated by Mozilla for MFSA 2026-57 and MFSA 2026-58. Individual issues range from low to high.
- Description: Mozilla fixed memory-safety issues, sandbox escapes, use-after-free bugs, privilege escalation, and JIT/compiler-related flaws that could expose users to code execution, sandbox escape, information disclosure, or denial-of-service risks when processing crafted content.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list explicitly includes Mozilla Firefox, and Mozilla's advisories name Firefox and Firefox ESR directly.
- Sources: Mozilla MFSA 2026-57 https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-57/; Mozilla MFSA 2026-58 https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-58/

**Finding 2: Ubuntu security notices published on June 16**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: New Ubuntu Security Notices on June 16, including USN-8438-1 OpenImageIO vulnerabilities, USN-8437-1 rabbitmq-c vulnerabilities, USN-8433-1 OpenStack Keystone vulnerabilities, USN-8432-1 FreeRDP vulnerabilities, and USN-8349-3 rsync regression.
- Severity: Not consistently stated in the Ubuntu notice index.
- Description: The June 16 Ubuntu notices include fixes for several packaged components. Notable items include FreeRDP CVE-2026-45700, where memory handling could lead to denial of service or arbitrary code execution, and rabbitmq-c issues including CVE-2026-44235 and CVE-2026-44236, which could cause denial of service or possibly code execution in the AMQP client library.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list explicitly includes Ubuntu. The rabbitmq-c notice may also matter in environments using RabbitMQ client tooling, though it is not the RabbitMQ server itself.
- Sources: Ubuntu Security Notices index https://ubuntu.com/security/notices; USN-8437-1 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8437-1; USN-8432-1 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8432-1

**Possible matches needing review**

- Product: Cisco product family, but not the exact monitored Cisco products
- Issue: CVE-2026-20262, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager arbitrary file write / path traversal vulnerability
- Severity: Medium in Cisco's advisory; CVSS v4.0 score 7.1 appears in public reporting.
- Description: Cisco and national CERT reporting state that Catalyst SD-WAN Manager is affected and that exploitation has been observed.
- Why review is needed: The monitored Cisco entries are Cisco Nexus, Cisco UCS, and Cisco Fabric Extender. The affected product is Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, so this should only be escalated if that product is also deployed.
- Sources: Cisco advisory https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ; Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-602 https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/cisco-security-advisory-av26-602; CISA KEV catalog https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog

- Product: Fortinet product family, but not FortiGate/FortiOS
- Issue: Active exploitation reported for FortiSandbox vulnerabilities CVE-2026-39813, CVE-2026-39808, and CVE-2026-25089
- Severity: Critical for the FortiSandbox issues discussed in the sources; Fortinet lists CVE-2026-39808 as Critical with CVSS 9.1.
- Description: Public reporting on June 16 says attackers are exploiting several FortiSandbox vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated privilege escalation or remote command execution.
- Why review is needed: The monitored Fortinet entry is Fortigate/FortiOS. FortiSandbox is a separate Fortinet product, so this is relevant only if FortiSandbox is present in the environment.
- Sources: BleepingComputer https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-fortinet-fortisandbox-flaws-now-exploited-in-attacks/; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-100 https://www.fortiguard.com/psirt/FG-IR-26-100

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Firefox and Ubuntu exposure, especially systems that process untrusted web content or remote desktop/client-library traffic. The Cisco SD-WAN Manager and FortiSandbox items should be checked against the actual deployed inventory before escalation because their product mapping is adjacent rather than direct.
